title: Vouching and cut-off
minutesWhy: law §3.3 row: vouch 20 purchase bills against PO, GRN and ledger
learn: What to check on a bill, its PO, GRN and ledger entry
How delivery terms and receipt date, not bill date, decide the year
What a cut-off error does to stock and profit
do: Draft the query mail to the client

case.role: First-year article assistant on the statutory audit
case.client: Tamhini Drivetech Private Limited, a Chakan company that makes gears, shafts and hubs for vehicle makers
case.team: Aditi Rane (senior), Rehan Siddiqui (manager), Sudha Venkatesh (partner)
case.goal: Check that the purchases booked around 31 March are in the right year, were approved and are billed correctly.
case.where: Accounts room, Chakan plant · Monday 19 April 2027

messages: Pallavi in accounts has put out the 20 purchase bills I picked from either side of 31 March. Vouch each against its PO, GRN and ledger entry.
Cut-off first, then approval, rate, quantity and GST. Rehan reviews purchases today, so notes by lunch, please.

documents.title: Purchase procedure · extract
documents.letterhead:
Tamhini Drivetech Private Limited
Plot B-47, Chakan Industrial Area Phase II, MIDC, Mahalunge, Pune 410501
documents.subject: Purchase procedure (extract)
body: Every purchase of goods or job work needs a purchase order (PO), approved before it goes to the vendor:
A change in rate or quantity needs a written amendment, approved at the same level.
Security records every vehicle in the gate inward register. Stores make a goods receipt note (GRN) for each delivery, and QC records any rejection on it.
Rejected goods go back to the vendor with a debit note within seven days.
Accounts book a bill only after matching it with the approved PO and the GRN, in the month the goods were received.

items.label: Bill 3 · Ghanekar Alloy Steels
items.note: Bill 3: second lot of the March schedule. Rates match the PO, the MD approved it, and 21,000 kg came in on 27 March and was booked that day. Fine.

items.note: Bill 6: the CNMG inserts are ₹7 above the PO, but amendment 1 of 18 March revised the rate and the MD approved it. Quantities match the GRN. Fine.

tasks.title: Draft the query mail to Mahesh
tasks.prompt: Aditi wants one mail to Mahesh Kadam, the accounts head, with a query for each exception other than the two cut-offs, which she will send herself. Pick the right line for each bill.
hints: Each problem is fixed by whoever caused it: the vendor corrects its own bill, Tamhini raises the debit note for what its QC rejected, and Rohit answers for his PO.

options.text: Bill 2 (Phillaur, PF/2026-27/2614): the GSTIN printed is 03UBZCP4179S1ZJ, but their registration is 03UBZCP4197S1ZJ. Please get a corrected invoice from Phillaur; until then the ₹65,520 credit is at risk.
options.why: A wrong supplier GSTIN is fixed by the supplier, with a corrected document. Until then the credit is at risk, not lost.

options.text: Bill 2 (Phillaur, PF/2026-27/2614): the GSTIN printed is 03UBZCP4179S1ZJ, not their 03UBZCP4197S1ZJ, so the ₹65,520 credit is lost for good. Please reverse it and pay Phillaur only ₹3,64,000.
options.why: Too far. Nothing is lost while Phillaur can still correct the bill, and Phillaur is still owed the GST it charged.

options.text: Bill 2 (Phillaur, PF/2026-27/2614): two digits of the GSTIN are swapped, but the PAN printed on the bill is right, so the bill can be passed as it is and the credit kept.
options.why: The bill must carry the supplier’s correct GSTIN. A right PAN elsewhere on the page does not fix it.

options.text: Bill 5 (Moshi, MC/26-27/286): the bill charges 6% + 6% on ₹1,15,200 of corrugated boxes, as Moshi’s bills did before September 2025, so the bill is fine as it is and can be paid in full.
options.why: That was the old rate. Corrugated boxes moved from 12% to 5% from 22 September 2025, and Tamhini’s own PO says 5%.

options.text: Bill 5 (Moshi, MC/26-27/286): the bill charges 6% + 6% where your PO says 5%. Please send all the 1,200 boxes back to Moshi and ask for a fresh supply on a new bill at 5% GST.
options.why: The boxes are fine. Only the tax on the bill is wrong, and the supplier can correct that.

options.text: Bill 5 (Moshi, MC/26-27/286): corrugated boxes are at 5% GST and your PO says 5%, but the bill charges 6% + 6%. Please ask Moshi to correct the bill and hold back the extra ₹8,064 till then.
options.why: The supplier corrects its own bill, and Tamhini pays only the tax that is due.

options.text: Bill 7 (Kolak, KP/26-27/1342): the PO for the VCI bags and film has no approval. Please have Rohit sign it today and date it 10 March, the PO date, so that the file is complete.
options.why: Never. A backdated signature is a false record. If he approved it, he says so now, with today’s date.

options.text: Bill 7 (Kolak, KP/26-27/1342): the PO for the VCI bags and film has no approval. Please ask Rohit to confirm in writing whether he approved this purchase, and why the PO went out unsigned.
options.why: We want the truth on file: who approved it and when. The answer goes into our controls note.

options.text: Bill 7 (Kolak, KP/26-27/1342): the goods, rate and bill all match the PO, so the blank approval box does not matter. Nothing is needed from Rohit on this one.
options.why: It matters. Approval is the control that stops unauthorised buying, even when the amount is right.

options.text: Bill 9 (Vishwamitri, VB/2627/4417): QC rejected 60 of the 1,200 bearings (6306-ZZ), but they are already booked. Please keep them in stock and use them where you can.
options.why: Rejected goods are not usable stock. They go back, and the debit note reverses what was booked.

options.text: Bill 9 (Vishwamitri, VB/2627/4417): QC rejected 60 of the 1,200 bearings (6306-ZZ). Please leave this year’s entry as it is and make a provision for ₹18,974.40 next year, when they go back.
options.why: The rejection happened in March, so March purchases must come down. A provision next year does not do that.

options.text: Bill 9 (Vishwamitri, VB/2627/4417): QC rejected 60 of the 1,200 bearings (6306-ZZ), yet the full bill is booked. Please raise the debit note for ₹18,974.40 and send the 60 back.
options.why: The debit note takes the rejected 60 out of March purchases and the vendor’s balance, as the PO terms say.

options.text: Bill 10 (Palar, PSG/0938/26-27): the 45 × 62 × 8 seals are billed at ₹39.50 against your PO rate of ₹38.00. The difference is only ₹1.50 a seal, so please pass the bill as it is.
options.why: It is ₹10,620 on one bill, and an unapproved price is an exception whatever its size.

options.text: Bill 10 (Palar, PSG/0938/26-27): the 45 × 62 × 8 seals are billed at ₹39.50 against your PO rate of ₹38.00, with no amendment. Please get Palar’s credit note for ₹10,620, or an amendment the MD has approved.
options.why: Either the price goes back to the PO, or someone with authority approves the change in writing.

options.text: Bill 10 (Palar, PSG/0938/26-27): the 45 × 62 × 8 seals are billed at ₹39.50 against your PO rate of ₹38.00. Please change your PO rate to ₹39.50 so that the PO matches the bill and it can be paid.
options.why: That bends the control to fit the bill. A change needs a proper amendment, approved by the right person.
